foe_from_flow — DRIVE ttc op

• Data kinds: image2d × image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.foe_from_flow(u, v, mask=None, *, min_speed: 'float' = 0.3, max_speed: 'float' = inf, iters: 'int' = 5, angle_scale: 'float' = 0.05) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import drivettc; drivettc.foe_from_flow(u, v, mask=None, *, min_speed: 'float' = 0.3, max_speed: 'float' = inf, iters: 'int' = 5, angle_scale: 'float' = 0.05) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("foe_from_flow"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Estimates the focus of expansion (FoE) from optical flow: {"foe": (col, row), "n", "residual"}.

The flow of pure translation is radial from the FoE (Longuet-Higgins & Prazdny 1980), so every pixel's flow line (the line through point p_i in the direction of the flow) passes through the FoE. FoE = the point minimising Σ w_i·dist(F, flow line_i)² (2×2 normal equations). The weights are iteratively 1/|p_i − F|·1/(1 + (角度残差/angle_scale)²) (Cauchy-like). The farther the pixel, the more the error in its flow-line direction affects the FoE position, so we divide by distance, and outliers (occlusion, textureless areas) are suppressed by the angle residual. The entry point (round 16) that derives from the flow the FoE treated as "known" in round 15. Theorem gate: feeding the true flow (flow_from_depth_motion) matches foe_from_motion to 1e-9.

mask selects the pixels to use (default = pixels that are finite with speed in [min_speed, max_speed]). Fewer than 3 valid pixels, or singular normal equations (all flow lines parallel), raise ValueError.
